chunks: Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man poured hot water on another man's head, so his hair fell out and never grew back. He said: “The diyyah is upon him.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation for bodily injury or loss
key_terms.رَأْسِ رَجُلٍ: the head of a man, the injured bodily area in this case
key_terms.لَا يَنْبُتُ أَبَدًا: it never grows back; permanent loss

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if hot water causes someone’s hair to fall out permanently?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bodily injury. If someone pours hot water on another person’s head and causes permanent loss of hair, he is liable for the diyyah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5330 - It is narrated from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who poured hot water on another man's head, causing his hair to fall out and never grow back.
Imam (as) said: "He must pay the full blood money (diyyah)."
